classification.difficultyReason: Identify the square's side as a radius and subtract the enclosed quadrant from the square.

content.prompt: The circle in the diagram has centre $A$ and radius $2\text{ cm}$. If $ABCD$ is a square, find the area of the shaded region. Give your answer in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: A full circle centred at A, with square ABCD extending right and down. B and D lie on the circle, AD is labelled 2 cm, and only the region between BC, CD and the quadrant arc BD is shaded. Ordinary source blue strokes and the red centre marker become black; meaningful lavender shading becomes house light purple.
spec.mathematics: AB = AD = BC = CD = 2 cm. The portion of the circle inside the square is a quadrant centred at A.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the requested shaded region are visible; no solution annotations or area answer.

answer.short:
$(4-\pi)\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the quadrant's area from the square's area.
answer.worked:
The square has side length $2\text{ cm}$. Since $ABCD$ is a square, the circle occupies a quadrant inside it.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=2\times2\\A_{\text{square}}&=4\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{quadrant}}&=\frac14\times\pi\times2^2\\A_{\text{quadrant}}&=\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=A_{\text{square}}-A_{\text{quadrant}}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=(4-\pi)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
